name: brutal
note: Risk-brutal: bigger office bonuses, so the leader's advantage compounds hard. §16 calls hand size against office bonuses the single biggest tuning knob.

placeholders.resolution.tieBreak: §9 says only 'higher total wins'. Even break is what makes edge 0 exactly 50%; a table needs a real rule.
placeholders.primaryGeneral.extremistPrimary: §9 says extremism is a primary bonus and general penalty but prints no magnitude.
placeholders.primaryGeneral.heterodoxPrimaryPenalty: §9 says heterodoxy is a primary penalty; no magnitude printed.
placeholders.primaryGeneral.crossBenchPrimaryPenalty: §9 lists cross-benching as a primary penalty; no magnitude printed.
placeholders.lean.decayFrequency: §16 open question 1 -- SETTLED 2026-08-31 by arithmetic, not simulation. Annual decay is -2 per cycle against a maximum push of +2, so sustained blowouts net zero and lean pins at 2 forever: realignment is impossible. Biennial (-1) against margin-based pushes accumulates. See engine/rules/lean.test.ts and reports/FINDINGS.md.
placeholders.lean.governorPushes: §16 open question; 'never' falls out of the priority rule, 'with-lean' is the alternative under test.
placeholders.lean.maxLean: No cap is stated. Without one, lean is unbounded.
placeholders.draft.districtsPerPack: §16 open: district-to-candidate ratio sets map fill rate and turn density.
placeholders.game.victory: §16 open question -- STILL OPEN, and now with evidence that none of §14's candidates works. Term-based conditions (two/three terms) terminate tightly but concentrate all value in one race: the SAME agent pool goes from 28% to 90% purely by switching points -> three-terms. Bills-passed keeps the field balanced (top 33%) but leaves 37-42% of games unfinished and runs to a median 34-49 years. Shipping points + a year cap as the least-bad playable default. See FINDINGS.md F16.
placeholders.economy.*: §13 describes the shape (random walk with memory, 2d6 roll-under on accumulated G) but prints no bounds or step sizes.
placeholders.legislature.reactionGoodOnRollAtLeast: §7/§12 say a reaction is rolled immediately on passage but do not say on what.
placeholders.hand.bonus*: §6 and §11 print these without saying per-seat or per-office. Read per seat they are a runaway: a player holding 20 Senate seats draws 32 cards a cycle. The doc's own 'base 12 with president +2 is a 17% edge' is 2/12, which only parses as per-office. Implemented per office held.
placeholders.game.victory (ties): §14 leaves the victory condition open and says nothing about ties on final score, which are common. Placeholder is a coin flip. Resolving by lowest seat -- the natural coding accident -- manufactures a 25pp seat bias that does not exist.
placeholders.game.deckOutEnds: §14 names deck-out as the ending, but also has defeated politicians circulate back through the draft. Circulation wins: talon+discard GROW from 79 to 273 cards over a hundred years, so deck-out is unreachable and cannot be the backstop the doc treats it as.
placeholders.lean.uncontestedPush: §10 says a push scales with how decisively a race was won and never says what a walkover does -- a race nobody contested has no margin at all. This is the single highest-leverage undecided rule in the design: 0 leaves the map a driftless random walk and the central thesis unimplemented; 1 produces genuine realignment. See FINDINGS.md F23 and F24.
placeholders.primaryGeneral.billCounterPips: §12 says a good reaction rewards yes-voters and a bad one penalises them at the next election, in both rounds, and that the card's accumulated counters are read off at resolution -- but prints no magnitude. One pip a counter is a stand-in.
